title: A Power Saving for Polynomial Differences at Prime Arguments
main_claim: Let h in Z[x] be prime-intersective (for every q it has a root r mod q with (r,q)=1), with degree at least 2 and positive leading coefficient. If A ⊆ [N] has no nonzero difference of the form h(p) with p prime, then |A| ≤ C_h N^{1-c_h}. The proof uses the companion Quasi-RH theorem: every Dirichlet L-function has no zero in Re s > 7/8.
coverage:
I checked every section except the lifts section (Sec. 4). That section is reproduced from the companion intersective-power paper, which the sibling branch at rank 428 already checked with no gap found; I only skimmed its statements. What I checked:
- Sec. 2: integrality of the auxiliary family; the identities T_l(Dx-i)=T_{lD}(x) and h_l(Dx-i)=λ(D)h_{lD}(x), which preserve prime arguments; local exponential sums (Weyl differencing mod p, Taylor and interpolation for p^j); uniform lifting classes; the zero-sum admissible cycle.
- Sec. 3: the tuple laws now use the allowed-regular weight W. I checked the covariance W_{lD}(y)=W_l(λ(D)y), the support of W lying in admissible residues, and that the mixing bound gives |Γ_p| ≤ p^{-γ}.
- Sec. 5, primes in progressions: radii in the Borel–Carathéodory step (17/16 < r < R < 9/8), the smoothed Mellin contour and residue, and the sharp differencing step with H = x^{31/32}, which gives an error uniform in the modulus.
- Sec. 5, minor arcs: exponents of the type I and type II sums after Vaughan's identity; the mixed-differencing coefficient θ=(k!)^2 b_k and the count of squarings, 2^{2k-1}.
- Sec. 6, kernel: placing q between Y^{η/4} and Y^{k-η/4} via Dirichlet approximation on minor arcs; the minor-arc bounds DH^2N^{-η} and DH^3N^{-ν}; the main term in reduced classes mod lb, where the factor φ(l)/l gives (x''-x')/n_b; local factorization of A_u, with a_{p,1}+b_{p,1}=Γ_p and a_{p,j}+b_{p,j}=0 for j ≥ 2; the bound when q_1 > H; all three major-arc error exponents; and the sign and normalization in the pair proposition.
- Sec. 7, descent: admissibility of a'_2-a'_1 at M_0 and at the conditioned primes; the progression-fiber identity; the bound ρ_l ≥ M_0^{1-L}; the bracket bound M_0^{s_0}(1-3ρ/4); and the induction with b_0=2a_0/ζ.

issues.description: The whole result depends on the companion Quasi-RH theorem: no zero of any Dirichlet L-function in Re s > 7/8, uniformly over moduli. This is a very strong, unrefereed input. The paper discloses the dependence, and the cited statement matches Thm 1.1 of the Sept 30 companion. The argument also goes through with that companion's weaker 11/12 stage (Thm 3.x).
issues.evidence: With 11/12 one takes σ0=23/24 and gets error Y^{47/48}. The kernel then needs 2η+4β+ζ < 1/(48k), and this holds because η=1/(10000k). The sibling branch at rank 149 checked the 11/12 version of the companion and found no gap.

sibling_notes: This paper adapts the companion intersective-power paper (rank 428, no_gap_found, same family 182) and the square-difference paper (rank 263). The lifts section and the reflection-positivity machinery are reused. What is new: the unit-root restriction in the weights and unit means, the factor φ(l)/l, the use of primes in progressions, and Vaughan's identity for the minor arcs over primes. All of these checked out.
